commands.review_summary:
The PR stamps the originating workflow URL into new apply-health snapshots, makes dashboard cards prefer that immutable URL over the mutable root status URL, and adds a focused precedence regression assertion.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows a retained apply-health snapshot can be paired with a later mutable root run URL, and the production screenshot plus linked run metadata corroborate the resulting misleading dashboard action.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The contributor must provide real after-fix behavior proof and remove the release-owned changelog entry; ClawSweeper automation cannot create proof from the contributor’s setup.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## Summary

Session-backed managed worktrees are now leased and Git-locked for the lifetime of every agent run. Idle GC and a separate non-force remover both reject an admitted run's checkout, including when the run uses a subdirectory inside the worktree.

## Root cause

GC's owner-activity read and `git worktree remove --force` were independent operations. The previous patch repeated the read closer to removal, but a session could still be admitted after that read and while the destructive command started.

## Fix

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease. `agent-command` acquires the lease before a session run touches its configured cwd and releases it in its outer cleanup. The lease retains the existing PID-tagged Git worktree lock, with local reference counting so only the final local holder unlocks it. All managed removal paths acquire the same queue through snapshotting and git removal; idle GC retains the owner-active guard after it has obtained that lease.

Lease lookup accepts a managed worktree root or one of its subdirectories, matching session worktrees whose configured workspace is nested below the repository root.

## Why this is the right boundary

The worktree service owns both the existing cross-process Git lock and destructive removal, so the same lifecycle primitive protects local and separate-service callers. Agent command is the session-run admission point that has the resolved cwd and can retain ownership through the actual runtime. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics, while an agent that loses the race before admission fails before using a deleted cwd rather than running against it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: 25 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`: passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts`, and `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Structured local review: no accepted or actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session must not have its managed checkout removed by GC or a separate non-force remover while its agent run is using that checkout or a nested workspace within it.
Real environment tested: pristine main `6eb9a5ada23b20353da9ef8e9fe69881567ca74f` and this patch `a3ef803caf83510ddf845d0910b55a151f4b343a`, driving the production ManagedWorktreeService against real on-disk git worktrees and filesystem state.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a session-owned worktree, start a lease from a nested directory, attempt non-force removal through a second service instance, confirm that removal is rejected by the live Git lock, release the lease, then observe removal complete.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6eb9a5a)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: false
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: false
# AFTER (this patch a3ef803)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: true
removal completes after the active run ends: true
```
Observed result after fix: a live session retains its nested working directory and blocks non-force removal until its lease ends, after which cleanup can complete normally.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the production worktree lifecycle and real git filesystem operations were exercised in-process.
